questions.stem: For a first-order reaction, the time required for $99.9\%$ completion is how many times the half-life ($t_{1/2}$) of the reaction?
questions.solution:
For first order reaction:
$t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{100 - x}$
$t_{99.9} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{0.1} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(10^3) = 3 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$.
Since $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k} \approx \frac{2.303 \log 2}{k} \approx 0.3 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$.
Therefore, $\frac{t_{99.9}}{t_{1/2}} = \frac{3}{0.3} = 10$.

questions.stem:
The rate constant of a first order reaction is $2.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. If the initial concentration of the reactant is $0.10\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$, the concentration of the reactant remaining after $100\ \mathrm{minutes}$ is $x \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$. The value of $x$ is ____________. (Nearest integer)
(Given: $e^{-1.2} = 0.301$)
questions.solution:
For first order reaction, $[A]_t = [A]_0 e^{-kt}$.
$k = 2.0 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$, $t = 100\ \mathrm{min} = 6000\ \mathrm{s}$.
$kt = 2.0 \times 10^{-4} \times 6000 = 1.2$.
$[A]_t = 0.10 \times e^{-1.2} = 0.10 \times 0.301 = 0.0301\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}} = 3.01 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mol\ L^{-1}}$.
Thus, $x \approx 3$.

questions.stem: A first-order reaction has a rate constant $k = 4.606 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$. The time required for the concentration of reactant to decrease from $2.0\ \mathrm{g}$ to $0.2\ \mathrm{g}$ is:
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction:
$t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{[A]_0}{[A]_t}\right)$
$t = \frac{2.303}{4.606 \times 10^{-3}} \log\left(\frac{2.0}{0.2}\right) = 0.5 \times 10^3 \log(10) = 500\ \mathrm{s}$.

questions.stem:
For a first order reaction, the time required for $50\%$ completion is $30\ \mathrm{min}$ at $300\ \mathrm{K}$ and $10\ \mathrm{min}$ at $320\ \mathrm{K}$. The activation energy $E_a$ for the reaction is ___________ $\mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$. (Nearest integer)
[Use: $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$, $\ln 3 = 1.0986$]
questions.solution:
$k = \frac{\ln 2}{t_{1/2}} \implies \frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{(t_{1/2})_1}{(t_{1/2})_2} = \frac{30}{10} = 3$
Using Arrhenius equation: $\ln\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{E_a}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2}\right)$
$1.0986 = \frac{E_a}{8.314} \left(\frac{320-300}{300 \times 320}\right) = \frac{E_a}{8.314} \left(\frac{20}{96000}\right) = \frac{E_a}{8.314 \times 4800}$
$E_a = 1.0986 \times 8.314 \times 4800 \approx 43842.6\ \mathrm{J\ mol^{-1}} \approx 44\ Cortical\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion of the reaction is $x$ times the time required for $90\%$ completion of the reaction. The value of $x$ is:

A first order reaction has a rate constant of $1.5 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. The time required for $5\ \mathrm{g}$ of this reactant to reduce to $3\ \mathrm{g}$ is _________ $\mathrm{s}$. (Round off to the nearest integer) [Given: $\log_{10} 3 = 0.4771$, $\log_{10} 5 = 0.6990$]
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction:
$t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \left(\frac{a_0}{a}\right)$
$t = \frac{2.303}{1.5 \times 10^{-3}} \log \left(\frac{5}{3}\right)$
$t = \frac{2303}{1.5} (0.6990 - 0.4771) = 1535.33 \times 0.2219 \approx 340.69 \approx 341\ \mathrm{s}$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion of the reaction is $x$ times the half-life ($t_{1/2}$) of the reaction. The value of $x$ is approximately:
questions.solution:
For first order reaction, $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100-y}\right)$.
$t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{1}\right) = \frac{4.606}{k}$.
$t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}$.
$\frac{t_{99\%}}{t_{1/2}} = \frac{4.606}{0.693} \approx 6.6$.

questions.stem:
For a first-order chemical reaction, the rate constant is $y\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. The time taken for the reactant concentration to decrease to $\frac{1}{10}$th of its initial concentration is $\frac{x}{y}$. The value of $x$ is _________ (Nearest integer).
(Given: $\ln 10 = 2.303$)
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, $t = \frac{1}{k} \ln\left(\frac{A_0}{A_t}\right)$.
Here, $A_t = \frac{A_0}{10}$ and $k = y\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$.
$t = \frac{1}{y} \ln(10) = \frac{2.303}{y}$.
Given $t = \frac{x}{y}$, we have $x = 2.303 \approx 2$ (Nearest integer).

questions.stem: For a first-order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion is about $x$ times the time required for $90\%$ completion. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100 - p}\right)$.
$t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{1}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 2$
$t_{90\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{10}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 1$
Therefore, $t_{99\%} = 2 \times t_{90\%} \implies x = 2$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion is $x$ times the time required for $90\%$ completion of the reaction. The value of $x$ is _______. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{a}{a-x}\right)$
$t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100-99}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(100) = 2 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$
$t_{90\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100-90}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(10) = 1 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$
Therefore, $t_{99\%} / t_{90\%} = 2$.
Thus, $x = 2$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion of the reaction is $x$ times the half-life ($t_{1/2}$) of the reaction. The value of $x$ is (nearest integer):
questions.solution:
For first order kinetics:
$t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100-y}\right)$
$t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{1}\right) = \frac{4.606}{k}$
$t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}$
$x = \frac{t_{99\%}}{t_{1/2}} = \frac{4.606}{0.693} \approx 6.65 \approx 7$.

questions.stem:
For a first order reaction, the time taken for $50\%$ completion is $30\ \mathrm{min}$ at $300\ \mathrm{K}$. If the activation energy of the reaction is $5.4\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}$, the time taken for $50\%$ completion at $350\ \mathrm{K}$ is _________ $\mathrm{min}$. (Nearest integer)
[Given: $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}}$, $\ln 2 = 0.693$]
questions.solution:
For first order, $t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} \implies \frac{t_{1/2}(300\ \mathrm{K})}{t_{1/2}(350\ \mathrm{K})} = \frac{k_{350}}{k_{300}}$.
Using Arrhenius equation: $\ln\left(\frac{k_{350}}{k_{300}}\right) = \frac{E_a}{R}\left(\frac{1}{300} - \frac{1}{350}\right) = \frac{5400}{8.314} \times \frac{50}{105000} \approx 649.5\ \times 0.000476 = 0.3093$.
Therefore, $\frac{k_{350}}{k_{300}} = e^{0.3093} \approx 1.3625$.
Thus, $t_{1/2}(350\ \mathrm{K}) = \frac{30}{1.3625} \approx 22.02\ \mathrm{min}$.
Rounding to the nearest integer gives 22.

A first order reaction has a rate constant $k = 3.38 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$ at $350\ \mathrm{K}$. The time required for $90\%$ completion of this reaction is __________ seconds. (Nearest integer)
(Given: $\log_{10}(10) = 1.0$)
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction:
$t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log_{10}\left(\frac{100}{100-90}\right) = \frac{2.303}{3.38 \times 10^{-2}} \log_{10}(10)$
$t = \frac{2.303}{0.0338} \approx 68.13\ \mathrm{s}$
Rounding to the nearest integer, we get 68.

A first-order reaction has a rate constant $k = 1.15 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s^{-1}}$. How long will $5\ \mathrm{g}$ of this reactant take to reduce to $3\ \mathrm{g}$? (Given: $\log_{10} 5 = 0.6990$, $\log_{10} 3 = 0.4771$)
questions.solution:
For first order reaction, $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log_{10}\left(\frac{a}{a-x}\right)$.
$t = \frac{2.303}{1.15 \times 10^{-3}} \log_{10}\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) \approx 2000 \times (0.6990 - 0.4771)$
$= 2000 \times 0.2219 = 443.8\ \mathrm{s} \approx 444\ \mathrm{s}$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the time required for $99.9\%$ completion of the reaction is _____ times the time required for $50\%$ completion of the reaction. (Nearest integer)
For a first order reaction, the time required for $99.9\%$ completion is about how many times the half-life ($t_{1/2}$) of the reaction?
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{a}{a-x}\right)$.
For $99.9\%$ completion, $t_{99.9\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100-99.9}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(1000) = \frac{3 \times 2.303}{k}$.
Half-life $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k} = \frac{2.303 \log(2)}{k} \approx \frac{0.301 \times 2.303}{k}$.
Dividing the two equations gives $\frac{t_{99.9\%}}{t_{1/2}} = \frac{3}{0.301} \approx 10$.

questions.stem: The half-life for the decomposition of gaseous compound $A$ is $240\ \mathrm{s}$ when the gaseous pressure is $500\ \mathrm{Torr}$. When the pressure is $250\ \mathrm{Torr}$, the half-life is $4.0\ \mathrm{min}$. The order of the reaction is _________.
questions.solution:
We know $t_{1/2} \propto P_0^{1-n}$.
$t_{1/2}^{(1)} = 240\ \mathrm{s}$ at $P_0^{(1)} = 500\ \mathrm{Torr}$.
$t_{1/2}^{(2)} = 4.0\ \mathrm{min} = 240\ \mathrm{s}$ at $P_0^{(2)} = 250\ \mathrm{Torr}$.
Since the half-life remains unchanged ($240\ \mathrm{s}$) when the initial pressure is halved, $t_{1/2}$ is independent of initial pressure.
Thus, $1-n = 0 \implies n = 1$.

questions.stem: For a first-order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion is about how many times the time required for $90\%$ completion of the reaction?
questions.solution:
For first-order kinetics:
$t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100-99}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(100) = 2 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$
$t_{90\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100-90}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(10) = 1 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$
Thus, $t_{99\%} / t_{90\%} = 2$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion is _________ times the time required for $90\%$ completion of the reaction. (Nearest integer)
For a first order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion is about $x$ times the time required for $90\%$ completion. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction:
$t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{100}{100-a}$
$t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{100}{1} = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 2$
$t_{90\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \frac{100}{10} = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 1$
Therefore, $t_{99\%} = 2 \times t_{90\%}$, so $x = 2$.

questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100 - x}\right)$.
For $99\%$ completion: $t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{1}\right) = \frac{4.606}{k}$.
Half-life $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}$.
Ratio: $\frac{t_{99\%}}{t_{1/2}} = \frac{4.606}{0.693} \approx 6.64$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion is $x$ times the time required for $90\%$ completion of the reaction. The value of $x$ is ________. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{100 - p}$.
For $99\%$ completion: $t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{1} = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 2$.
For $90\%$ completion: $t_{90\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{10} = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 1$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the ratio of time required for $99.9\%$ completion to the time required for $50\%$ completion of the reaction is approximately:
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction:
$t_{99.9\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{100-99.9}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(10^3) = 3 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$
$t_{50\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\left(\frac{100}{50}\right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(2) \approx 0.3 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$
$\frac{t_{99.9\%}}{t_{50\%}} = \frac{3}{0.301} \approx 10$.

questions.stem: For a first order reaction, the ratio of time taken for $75\%$ completion to that of $50\%$ completion is _______ . (Nearest integer)
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the half-life $t_{50\%} = \frac{\ln 2}{k}$.
The time for $75\%$ completion $t_{75\%}$ is equivalent to two half-lives because $100\% \to 50\% \to 25\%$.
Thus, $t_{75\%} = 2 \times t_{50\%}$.
The ratio $\frac{t_{75\%}}{t_{50\%}} = 2$.

questions.stem: For a first-order reaction, the time required for $99.9\%$ completion is approximately how many times the half-life ($t_{1/2}$) of the reaction?
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \frac{100}{100 - x} \right)$.
For $99.9\%$ completion:
$t_{99.9\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log \left( \frac{100}{0.1} \right) = \frac{2.303}{k} \log(10^3) = 3 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$.
Since $t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k} \approx \frac{2.303 \log 2}{k} \approx 0.301 \times \frac{2.303}{k}$,
$t_{99.9\%} \approx \frac{3}{0.301} \times t_{1/2} \approx 10\, t_{1/2}$.

questions.stem: A first order reaction has a rate constant $1.15 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}$. How many seconds will it take for $5\text{ g}$ of this reactant to reduce to $3\text{ g}$? [Given: $\log_{10} 5 = 0.699$, $\log_{10} 3 = 0.4771$]
questions.solution:
For first order kinetics: $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log_{10}\left(\frac{a}{a-x}\right)$.
$t = \frac{2.303}{1.15 \times 10^{-3}} \log_{10}\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) = 2002.6 \times (0.6990 - 0.4771) = 2002.6 \times 0.2219 = 444.38\text{ s}$.
Rounding to the nearest integer, we get 444.

questions.stem: For a first-order reaction, the time required for $99.9\%$ completion of the reaction is approximately how many times the half-life ($t_{1/2}$) of the reaction?

For a first order reaction, the time required for $99\%$ completion is $x$ times the time required for the completion of $90\%$ of the reaction. The value of $x$ is _________. (Round off to the nearest integer)
questions.solution:
For first order kinetics: $t = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{100 - a\%}$.
$t_{99\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{1} = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 2$
$t_{90\%} = \frac{2.303}{k} \log\frac{100}{10} = \frac{2.303}{k} \times 1$
Therefore, $t_{99\%} = 2 \times t_{90\%}$.
Thus, $x = 2$.
